sections.title: Design Examples: Settlement for Static Analysis
sections.body:
[p. 338] Design examples provided in this appendix are described below. The evaluation of ultimate limit states for these same design examples are provided in Appendix B. No examples of secondary settlement (creep) are presented in this appendix.

Example C-1 Settlement of isolated footing on clay (e-log-p method).
Example C-2 Settlement due to superimposed foundation loads on clay (e-log-p method).
Example C-3a Settlement of soft clay due to areal fill load only (e-log-p method).
Example C-3b Settlement of soft clay layer due to areal fill and isolated footing (e-log-p method).
Example C-3c Time required to obtain 1 inch or less of settlement due to areal fill and foundation placed on soft clay (e-log-p method).
Example C-4 Recompression settlement of isolated footing on clay (e-log-p method).
Example C-5 Settlement of isolated footing on clay (PMT method).
Example C-6a Settlement of isolated footing on mixed soils (DMT Incremental Constrained Modulus method).
Example C-6b Comparison of dilatometer constrained modulus MDMT with laboratory oedometer constrained modulus M.
Example C-7a Settlement of isolated footing on sand (DMT Incremental Constrained Modulus method).
Example C-7b Settlement of isolated footing on sand (Ménard and Rousseau PMT method).
Example C-7c Settlement of isolated footing on sand (Schmertmann’s method for cohesionless soils).
Example C-7d Settlement of isolated footing on sand (Burland and Burbidge SPT method for sands and gravels).

[p. 352] Given: Prior to constructing the footings, site grades are raised 8.0 ft by placing areal fill throughout the entire site, including beneath the building (see Figure C-3). The fill material placed beneath the building and 10 ft beyond the building limits consists of well-compacted, engineered fill (assume structural fill will not settle due to the induced loadings from the footings). Estimate the following:

[p. 353] Figure C-3. Foundation and soil conditions for Example C-3

[p. 354] Table C-3a Solution for settlement of soft clay layer due to areal fill loading only
Step 1 | e0, σ′p, Cc, and Cr are provided for each soil strata as illustrated in Figure C-3. Compute σ′z0 and σ′m for each Shelby tube sample.
paragraph 6-5a: σ′z0 = ∑γ · H − u
Eq. 6-4: σ′m = σ′p − σ′z0
Shelby #1: 7.0-ft depth (Strata 1):
σ′z0 = ((7.0 ft · 120 pcf) − (2.0 ft · 62.4 pcf))/2,000 = 0.36 tsf
σ′m = 1.0 tsf − 0.36 tsf = 0.64 tsf
Shelby #2: 15.0-ft depth (Strata 2):
σ′zo = ((10.0 ft · 120 pcf) + (5.0 ft · 125 pcf) − (10.0 ft · 62.4 pcf))/2,000 = 0.60 tsf
σ′m = 6.0 tsf − 0.60 tsf = 5.4 tsf
Step 2 | Divide the soil beneath the foundation into layers where the soil parameters are constant. The top layer should be at the base of the areal fill and the bottom layer should extend to an incompressible layer, or until the increase in the induced vertical stress Δσzfill is negligible, resulting in small acceptable increases in settlement, whichever is deeper. Settlements will be estimated to a depth of 25 ft below existing grade, where a very dense clayey sand is encountered.
Step 3 | Compute initial vertical effective stress (σ′z0) at the midpoint of each layer per paragraph 6-5a.
σ′z0 = ∑γ · H − u
Step 4 | From the overionization margin (σ′m) computed for each soil strata, compute the preconsolidation stress (σ′p) at the midpoint of each layer per Eq. 6-4.
σ′p = σ′m + σ′z0
Step 5 | Compute the areal fill load (P) at the center line of the areal fill.
P = γmfill · Hfill = (135 pcf · 8.0 ft)/2,000 = 0.54 tsf

sections.body:
[p. 364] Given: An 8.0-ft by 8.0-ft isolated spread footing supporting a 150-ton column load bearing 2.5 ft below grade on the clay profile illustrated in Figure C-5. TEXAM PMT conducted in clay soils as illustrated in Figure C-5. Groundwater was not encountered. Assume secondary settlement is negligible.

[p. 365] Figure C-5. Settlement of isolated footing on clay (pressuremeter test method)

[p. 366] Table C-5 Solution for settlement of isolated footing on clay (pressuremeter test method) per Table 7-5
Step 1 | PMT modulus E0 per depth from the corrected pressuremeter test curve for each PMT test is illustrated in Figure C-5.
Step 2 & 3 | Compute the gross bearing pressure q (or qeq) at the base of the footing per paragraph 5-2b. The ultimate bearing capacity with a factor of safety of 3 exceeds the gross bearing pressure as illustrated in Appendix B, Example B-5.
q = (Q + Wf)/A − uD = (150 T + [(150 pcf)/2,000 · (8.0 ft)^2 · 2.5 ft])/((8.0 ft)^2) − 0 = 2.53 tsf
Step 4 | Choose the lesser of the values from Steps 2 and 3 for estimating settlements per Eq. 7-11. Therefore, q = 2.53 tsf.
Step 5 | Compute the vertical effective stress at the bearing elevation of the footing (σ′zD).
σ′zD = ((2.5 ft · 125 pcf))/2,000 = 0.156 tsf
Step 6 | Divide the soil beneath the foundation into sixteen elementary layers of B/2 thickness to a depth of 8B (64 ft) below the foundation and combine these sixteen elementary layers into five distinct layers, E1, E2, E3/4/5, E6/7/8, and E9/16 as illustrated in Figure 7-12.
Step 7 | Compute the average pressuremeter modulus of each of the five combined distinct layers (E1, E2, E3/4/5, E6/7/8, and E9/16) per Step 6 by the harmonic mean technique per Eq. Figure 7-13.
Eq. 7-13: Ek = n/(1/(E 1)+ 1/(E 2)+⋯+ 1/(E n))
Layer E1: B/2 below footing (4 ft below footing): E1 = 225 tsf
Layer E2: B/2 to B below footing (4 to 8 ft below footing):
2/E2 = 1/(225tsf) + 1/(292tsf); therefore, E2 = 254 tsf
Layer E3/4/5: B to 2.5B below footing (8 to 20 ft below footing):
7/(E3/4/5) = 1/(292 tsf) + 1/(394 tsf) + 1/(25 tsf) + 1/(33 tsf) + 1/(52 tsf) + 1/(349 tsf) + 1/(287 tsf)
therefore, E3/4/5 = 69 tsf
Layer E6/7/8: 2.5B to 4B below footing (20 to 32 ft below footing):
3/(E6/7/8) = 1/(287 tsf) + 1/(678 tsf) + 1/(1,071 tsf); therefore, E6/7/8 = 509 tsf
Layer E9/16: 4B to 8B below footing (32 to 64 ft below footing):
2/(E9/16) = 1/(1,220 tsf) + 1/(1,724 tsf); therefore, E9/16 = 1,429 tsf
Step 8 | Compute the average pressuremeter modulus within the zone of influence of the spherical tensor (Ec) to a depth of 0.5B (first layer) below the footing bearing elevation. Therefore,
Ec = E1 = 225 tsf from Step 7.
[p. 367]
Step 9 | Compute the equivalent distortion modulus (Ed) within the zone of influence of the deviatoric tensor to a depth of 8B (16 layers beneath the footing bearing elevation per Step 6) per Eq. 7-14:
Eq. 7-14: 1/(E d) = (1/4) (1/(E 1) + 1/(0.85E 2) + 1/(E 3/4/5) + 1/(2.5E 6/7/8) + 1/(2.5E 9/16))
where:
E1, E2, E3/4/5, E6/7/8, and E9/16 are computed by harmonic mean method, Step 7.
1/Ed = (1/4)(1/E1 + 1/(0.85E2) + 1/(E3/4/5) + 1/(2.5E6/7/8) + 1/(2.5E9/16))
1/Ed = (1/4)(1/(225 tsf) + 1/(0.85 · 254 tsf) + 1/(69 tsf) + 1/(2.5 · 509 tsf) + 1/(2.5 · 1429 tsf))
Therefore, Ed = 162tsf.
Step 10 | Obtain the rheological factor ∝d and ∝c from Table 7-6. α is determined based on the soil type and state of consolidation from the ratio of Ed/p*Le and Ec/p*Le, respectively.
Ed/(p*Le) = (162 tsf)/(10.0 tsf) = 16.2 From
Table 7-6, ∝d= 1
Ec/(p*Le) = (225 tsf)/(10.0 tsf) = 22.5 From
Table 7-6, ∝c= 1
Step 11 | Obtain the deviatoric and spherical shape factors λd and λc from Figure 7-11. The shape factors are a function of the base length to width ratio L/B of the footing.
L/B = 1 From Figure 7– 11, λd and λc = 1.1
Step 12 | Estimate the total settlement per Eq. 7-11.
Eq. 7-11: δ = [(2/(9E d)) (q − σ′zD)B0 (λd (B/(B 0)))^αd] + [((∝ c)/(9E c)) (q − σ′zD)λc · B]
δ = [ 2/(9 · 162 tsf) · (2.53 tsf − 0.156 tsf) · 2.0 ft (1.1 · (8.0 ft)/(2.0 ft))^1 ]
+ [1/(9 · 225 tsf) · (2.53 tsf − 0.156 tsf) · 1.1 · 8.0 ft]
δ = 0.029 ft + 0.010 ft = 0.039 ft = 0.47 in
Step 13 | Compute the average pressuremeter modulus of each of the soft/loose layers by the harmonic mean technique per Eq. 7-15.
Eq. 7-15: EL = n/(1/(E 1)+ 1/(E 2)+⋯+ 1/(E n))
EL = 3/(1/25 + 1/33 + 1/52) = 33.5 tsf
[p. 368]
Step 14 | Compute the influence factor for vertical stress (Iσ) per Eq. 6-9 and corresponding induced vertical stress (Δσz) beneath the footing at the midpoint of each layer per Eq. 6-6.

Step 6 | Divide the soil beneath the foundation into sixteen elementary layers of B/2 thickness to a depth of 8B (64.0 ft) below the foundation and combine these sixteen elementary layers into five distinct layers, E1, E2, E3/4/5, E6/7/8, and E9/16 as illustrated in Figure 7-12.
Step 7 | Compute the average pressuremeter modulus of each of the five combined distinct layers (E1, E2, E3/4/5, E6/7/8, and E9/16) per step 6 by the harmonic mean technique per Eq. 7-13. Eq. 7-13: Ek = n/(1/(E 1)+ 1/(E 2)+⋯+ 1/(E n))
Layer E1: B/2 below footing (4 ft below footing):
E1 = 78 tsf
Layer E2: B/2 to B below footing (4 to 8 ft below footing):
2/E2 = 1/(78 tsf) + 1/(238 tsf); therefore, E2 = 118 tsf
Layer E3/4/5: B to 2.5B below footing (8 to 20 ft below footing):
3/(E3/4/5) = 1/(238 tsf) + 1/(320 tsf) + 1/(826 tsf); therefore, E3/4/5 = 351 tsf
Layer E6/7/8: 2.5B to 4B below footing (20 to 32 ft below footing):
2/(E6/7/8) = 1/(1,419 tsf) + 1/(1,065 tsf); therefore, E6/7/8 = 1,217 tsf
Layer E9/16: 4B to 8B below footing (32 to 64 ft below footing):
3/(E9/16) = 1/(2,508 tsf) + 1/(1,059 tsf) + 1/(1,128 tsf); therefore, E9/16 = 1,346 tsf
Step 8 | Compute the average pressuremeter modulus within the zone of influence of the spherical tensor Ec to a depth of 0.5B (first layer) below the footing bearing elevation. Therefore,
Ec = E1 = 78 tsf from Step 7.
[p. 382]
Step 9 | Compute the equivalent distortion modulus Ed within the zone of influence of the deviatoric tensor to a depth of 8B (16 layers beneath the footing bearing elevation per Step 6) per Eq. 7-14:
Eq. 7-14: 1/(E d) = (1/4) (1/(E 1) + 1/(0.85E 2) + 1/(E 3/4/5) + 1/(2.5E 6/7/8) + 1/(2.5E 9/16))
where:
E1, E2, E3/4/5, E6/7/8, and E9/16 are computed by the harmonic mean method, Step 7.
1/Ed = (1/4)(1/E1 + 1/(0.85E2) + 1/(E3/4/5) + 1/(2.5E6/7/8) + 1/(2.5E9/16))
1/Ed = (1/4)(1/(78 tsf) + 1/(0.85 · 118 tsf) + 1/(351 tsf) + 1/(2.5 · 1,217 tsf) + 1/(2.5 · 1,346 tsf))
Ed = 152 tsf
Step 10 | Obtain the rheological factor ∝d and ∝c from Table 7-6. α is determined based on the soil type and state of consolidation from the ratio of Ed/pne and Ec/pne, respectively. pne is calculated using Eq. 5-24.
Ed/pne = (152 tsf)/(8.5 tsf) = 9.5 from
Table 7-6, αd = 0.5
Ec/pne = (78 tsf)/(8.5 tsf) = 4.9 from
Table 7-6, αc = 0.33
Step 11 | Obtain the deviatoric and spherical shape factors λd and λc from Figure 7-11. The shape factors are a function of the base length-to-width ratio L/B of the footing.
L/B = 1; from Figure 7– 11, λd and λc = 1.1
Step 12 | Estimate the total settlement per Eq. 7-11.
δ = [ (2/(9Ed))(q − σ′zD)B0 · (λd (B/B0))^αd] + [ ((∝c)/(9Ec))(q − σ′zD)λc · B]
δ = [2/(9 · 152 tsf) · (3.31 tsf − 0.156 tsf) · 2.0ft · (1.1 · (8.0 ft)/(2.0 ft))^0.5]
+ [0.33/(9 · 78 tsf) · (3.31tsf − 0.156 tsf) · 1.1 · 8.0ft]
δ = 0.015 ft + 0.013 ft = 0.028 ft = 0.38 in
[Note (not printed): Table C-7c, Step 12 (p. 382): with the values in the line above, the first term is 2/(9 · 152) · (3.31 − 0.156) · 2.0 · (1.1 · 8.0/2.0)^0.5 = 0.019 ft, not 0.015 ft, and the total is 0.019 + 0.013 = 0.032 ft (0.39 in); 0.028 ft would be 0.34 in, not 0.38 in. The numbers above are as printed.]

[p. 384] Table C-7d Solution for settlement of isolated footing on sand using Schmertmann’s cone penetration test method
Step 1 | Measured tip resistance qc as a function of depth from CPT data is illustrated in Figure C-7a.
Step 2 | Determine the equivalent Young’s modulus Es per Eq. 7-16. Divide the soil beneath the bearing elevation into layers depending on the variation in Es versus depth.
Step 3 | Compute the gross bearing pressure q (or qeq) at the base of the footing per paragraph 5-2b. The ultimate bearing capacity with a factor of safety of 3 exceeds the gross bearing pressure as illustrated in Appendix B, Example B-7, Tables B-7a and B-7b.
q = (Q + Wf)/A − uD = (200 T + [(150 pcf)/2,000 · (8.0 ft)^2 · 2.5 ft])/((8.0 ft)^2) − 0 = 3.31 tsf
Step 4 | Compute the vertical effective stress at the bearing elevation of the footing (σ′zD).
σ′zD = ((2.5ft · 125 pcf))/2,000 = 0.156 tsf
Step 5 | Develop strain influence factor diagram below the base of the footing per Figure 7-13. Reference Figure C-7b.
Step 6 | Compute the peak strain influence factor (Izp) per Eq. 7-18:
Izp = 0.5 + 0.1√((q − σ′zD)/σ′zp)
Izp = 0.5 + 0.1√((3.31 tsf − 0.156 tsf)/(′) = 0.779)
6.5 × (125 pcf)/2,000
Step 7 | Compute embedment (C1) and creep correction (C2) factors per Eq. 7-24 and 7-25.
Eq. 7-24: C1 = 1 − 0.5 ((′ σ zD)/(′ q − σ z D)) ≥ 0.5
C1 = 1 − 0.5 ((0.156 tsf)/(3.31 tsf − 0.156 tsf)) = 0.975 ≥ 0.5
Eq. 7-25: C2 = 1 + 0.2 log10 (t/0.1)
C2 = 1 + 0.2 log10 (50/0.1) = 1.539
[p. 385]
Step 8 | Produce a table for each layer as follows within the strain influence factor diagram per Figure C-7b. Reference table in Step 10.
a. The number of the layer
b. Depth of the layer (feet)
c. Depth to the midpoint of each layer, z (feet)
d. The layer thickness in feet
e. qc (tsf) or N60 (bpf) values
f. Es (tsf)
g. Strain influence factor (Ia) for axisymmetric footing
h. ((I z · H)/(E s)) feet
Step 9 | Compute the vertical strain influence factor (Iza) at the midpoint of each layer per Eq. 7-19 and 7-20 for the axisymmetric footing. Reference Table in Step 10.
Eq. 7-19: Axisymmetric footings for z = 0 to 0.5B
Iza = 0.1 + (z/B) (2 · Izp − 0.2)
Eq. 7-20: Axisymmetric footings for z = 0.5B to 2B
Iza = 0.667 · Izp(2 − z/B)
Step 10 | Compute ((I z·H)/(E s)) at the midpoint of each layer and sum for the layers within the strain influence factor diagram per Figure C-7b.
Step 10 | ″ | Layer No. | Depth of Layer Below Footing (ft) | Depth at Layer Midpoint, z (ft) | Layer Thickness, H (ft) | Tip Resistance, qc(tsf) | Es (tsf) | Iz | (Iz · H)/Es
(ft^3/tons)
Step 10 | ″ | 1 | 0 to 1.5 | 0.75 | 1.5 | 100 | 250 | 0.227 | 0.0014
Step 10 | ″ | 2 | 1.5 to 2.5 | 2.0 | 1.0 | 100 | 250 | 0.439 | 0.0018
Step 10 | ″ | 3 | 2.5 to 4.0 | 3.25 | 1.5 | 160 | 400 | 0.651 | 0.0024
Step 10 | ″ | 4 | 4.0 to 7.5 | 5.75 | 3.5 | 100 | 250 | 0.665 | 0.0093
Step 10 | ″ | 5 | 7.5 to 9.5 | 8.5 | 2.0 | 300 | 750 | 0.489 | 0.0013
Step 10 | ″ | 6 | 9.5 to 12.5 | 11.0 | 3.0 | 160 | 400 | 0.324 | 0.0024
Step 10 | ″ | 7 | 12.5 to 16.0 | 14.25 | 3.5 | 200 | 500 | 0.114 | 0.008
Step 10 | ∑ (I ·H z)/(E s) = 0.0266
[p. 386]
Step 11 | Compute total settlement per Eq. 7-26.
δ = C1 · C2(q − σ′zD) ∑(Iz · H)/Es
δ = 0.975 · 1.539 · (3.31 tsf − 0.156 tsf) · 0.0266 (ft^3)/(tons) = 0.125 ft = 1.5 in
[Note (not printed): Table C-7d, Step 10 (p. 385): layer 7 gives (Iz · H)/Es = 0.114 · 3.5 ft/500 tsf = 0.0008 ft^3/ton, printed 0.008; with 0.0008 the sum is 0.0194, not 0.0266, and Step 11 (p. 386) gives δ = 0.975 · 1.539 · (3.31 tsf − 0.156 tsf) · 0.0194 = 0.092 ft (1.1 in), not 0.125 ft (1.5 in). The numbers above are as printed.]

Table C-7e Solution for settlement of isolated footing on sand using the Burland and Burbidge standard penetration test method for sands and gravels per Table 7-9
Step 1 | N60 data as a function of depth from SPT results is illustrated in Figure C-7a.
Step 2 | Compute the gross bearing pressure q (or qeq) at the base of the footing per paragraph 5-2b. The ultimate bearing capacity with a factor of safety of 3 exceeds the gross bearing pressure as illustrated in Appendix B, Example B-7, Tables B-7a and B-7b.
q = (Q + Wf)/A − uD = (200 T + [(150 pcf)/2,000 · (8.0 ft)^2 · 2.5 ft])/((8.0 ft)^2) − 0 = 3.31 tsf
Step 3 | Compute depth of influence (ZI) per Eq. 7-27.
ZI = 1.43B^0.7
ZI = 1.43 · 8.0^0.7 = 6.13 ft
Step 4 | Compute the arithmetic mean of the measured N60 values measured within the depth of influence ZI = 6.13 ft.
N̅60 = (12 + 15 + 14)/3 = 14 pf
Step 5 | Compute the soil compressibility index Ic per Eq. 7-28.
Ic = 0.35/(N̅60^1.4)
Ic = 0.35/(14^1.4) = 0.0087 tsf^(−1)
Step 6 | Compute shape (C1) layer thickness (C2) and time-dependent (C3) factors per Eq. 7-32, 7-33, and 7-34.
Eq. 7-32: C1 = [(1.25(L/B))/((L/B)+0.25)]^2 ≥ 1
Eq. 7-33: C2 = ((H s)/(Z I)) (2 − (H s)/(Z I)) ≤ 1
C2 = (6.13/6.13)(2 − 6.13/6.13) ≤ 1 = 1.0
Eq. 7-34: C3 = 1 + R3 + Rt · log10 (t/3)
C3 = 1 + 0.3 + 0.2 log10 (50/3) = 1.54
[p. 387]
Step 7 | Compute the average initial vertical effective stress (σ′zo) within depth of influence (ZI). Depth: 2.5 ft below grade:
σ′z0 = (2.5 ft · 125 pcf)/2,000 = 0.156 tsf
Depth: 8.63 ft below grade (2.5 ft + 6.13 ft):
σ′zo = (8.63 ft · 125 pcf)/2,000 = 0.539 tsf
σ̅′zo = (0.156 tsf + 0.539 tsf)/2 = 0.35 tsf
Step 8 | Compute the preconsolidation stress (σ′p) from Eq. 3-23.
Eq. 3-23: σ′p = 0.468Pa · N60^m
σ′p = 0.47 · 1.0 · 14^0.8 = 3.88 tsf
Step 9 | σ̅′zo = 0.35 tsf, σ′p = 3.88 tsf, and (q + σ̅′z0) = 3.31 tsf + 0.35 tsf = 3.66 tsf
Since σ̅′z0 ≠ σ′p and (q + σ̅′z0) ≤ σ′p, estimate settlements per Eq. 7-30.
Eq. 7-30: δ = C1 · C2 · C3(q + σ̅′z0)ZI ((I c)/3)
δ = 1.0 · 1.0 · 1.54 · (3.31 tsf + 0.35 tsf) · 6.13 ft · (0.0087 tsf^(−1))/3 = 0.10 ft = 1.2 in
